blk_part_01_how_a_language_exchange_work.text: A language exchange is a trade: you give something, and you get something. You help someone with your language, and they help you with theirs. For example, you speak Japanese and want to practise English. Then you look for an English speaker who wants to practise Japanese. Many language cafés split the time in half. You talk in one language for half an hour. Then you talk in the other language for half an hour. This way, both people get the same time to learn.

blk_part_03_introducing_yourself.text: In the Netherlands, people shake hands when they meet someone new. At the same time, they say their name: Hi! I'm Sanne. Often they say only their first name. In Japan, many people bow, or bend forward, and say their family name. But for Dutch people, a hello without a name is rude, or not polite. Why? Dutch people like to be clear, so they start with a name. When you hear a new name, you say your name too. Then you say: Nice to meet you.
